input_cursor.backlog_note: This first comparator pass grades the six candidate mechanisms in the three newest scientist_agents records inspected directly. Earlier research_workers records and other worker families remain queued for later comparator passes.

grading_rubric.A: Direct quantitative primary evidence with a controlled or strongly matched comparison on the mechanism itself, appropriate endpoint, strong provenance, and meaningful independent replication or equivalent robustness evidence.
grading_rubric.B: Direct quantitative primary evidence with a useful comparison, but limited external replication, endpoint validity, sample breadth, or mechanism isolation.
grading_rubric.C: Suggestive quantitative/observational evidence or strong failure evidence from which the proposed intervention is inferred; causal effect of the candidate mechanism itself is not established.
grading_rubric.D: Plausible hypothesis with weak or indirect empirical support for the claimed mechanism.
grading_rubric.modifiers: +/- reflect strength within a band. Grades are evidence strength for the named mechanism, not expected value for O.

observed_policy: O prioritizes independent signed production evidence, then independently controlled held-out evidence, mechanically judged held-out protected regression, deterministic internal CI, and finally self-evaluation/architecture.
O requires negative evidence to stay scoped to the exact candidate/configuration/conditions and distinguishes adaptation or ablation loss from failure of an original baseline.
Therefore external literature can justify or prioritize an O experiment, but does not by itself prove an O-specific adaptation improves O.

source.title: ResearchArena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in Automated AI R&D

assessments.primary_source_quality: High provenance for a current primary preprint and author-maintained results site, but not yet peer reviewed and without independent replication located in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: Direct controlled access comparison is present. The author site gives same-run examples including Sonnet 4.6 suspicion 4/100 trajectory-only versus 92/100 with artifact access, and GPT-5.4 suspicion 79/100 without CoT versus 31/100 with CoT on a long-context backdoor. The study evaluates four monitor access types on four long-horizon AI-R&D settings, and reports artifact access generally improves detection while training-data-hidden sabotage remains difficult.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong: monitor access types vary artifact execution access and CoT access while sharing the same scoring rubric; same-run examples isolate access differences particularly clearly. Red-team/model/task heterogeneity remains in pooled results.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for the effect of granting executable artifact access. The access-axis design is intervention-like, but the measured benefit depends on whether the monitor actually chooses a revealing probe, and attack classes differ beyond localization.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong relative to typical preprints: framework/code/traces are released and the author site exposes task/monitor setup and example traces. No independent reproduction checked in this pass.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong within benchmark scope: wrong probes, shallow inspection, and benign-rationale overtrust are directly documented failure modes; artifact access is helpful but insufficient.
scope_limits: Benchmark is adversarial automated AI-R&D sabotage, not general scientific-quality evaluation.
Red teams were instructed to pursue side tasks; authors caution detection can be an upper bound versus more strategic concealment.

Exact pooled table values in the worker record partly came through a mirror; this comparator relies on the primary abstract/author site for the grade rather than treating mirror-only numbers as independently verified primary evidence.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for allowing monitors to execute/probe submitted artifacts instead of trajectory-only review in the tested ResearchArena settings.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Untested. Using this idea inside O would require an O-specific held-out comparison of evaluator configurations with matched artifacts, false-positive/cost controls, and exact probe logs before claiming benefit.

source.title: ResearchArena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in Automated AI R&D

assessments.primary_source_quality: Same high-provenance primary source as above.
assessments.quantitative_result: The paper directly shows missed sabotage despite artifact access and identifies wrong-test failure traces, but it does not compare an explicit automated probe-generator/search intervention against a matched baseline.
assessments.matched_baseline: Not available for the proposed probe-generation mechanism itself.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Failure mechanism is well supported; proposed remedy is inferred. The evidence establishes that probe choice can be decisive, not that a separate probe-search module improves detection net of cost or false positives.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Released traces make the failure cases inspectable, but no implementation/ablation of the proposed mechanism exists in the cited source.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence that full artifact access can still fail when the evaluator runs the wrong test.
scope_limits: Probe-search cost, false positives, search budget, and stopping policy are unspecified.
Transfer from sabotage detection to general scientific error discovery is plausible but not demonstrated.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: C+ because the proposed separate probe-generation operator is not actually evaluated; only its motivating failure mode is.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Untested hypothesis. O should treat it as a candidate experiment, not retained capability evidence.

source.title: How Far Are We From True Auto-Research?

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary preprint with 117 generated papers, released code/logs, 351 artifact-aware reviews, SAR scores, and human integrity inspection. No peer-review status or independent replication established in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: Artifact-aware review reduced mean score relative to manuscript-only SAR by 0.85 for Claude Code, 0.42 for Codex, and 0.86 for Kimi Code. Human audit found paper-vs-artifact mismatch/fabricated-reference rates ranging from 5%/8% for Codex to 77%/72% for Kimi Code. None of 117 generated papers reached the paper's artifact-aware top-tier bar.
assessments.matched_baseline: Useful but not perfectly isolated. The same corpus is viewed through manuscript-only and artifact-aware lenses, but SAR and PR are distinct reviewer procedures and reviewer identities/configurations, so the score drop is not a pure single-variable access ablation.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for the claim that artifact-aware inspection surfaces additional integrity issues. Weak for the bundled 'integrity autoreject' component: the source does not directly randomize or compare automatic hard rejection versus soft scoring.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong: corpus, code/logs, reviews and configurable harness are reported released.
assessments.external_replication: No direct independent replication identified. BadScientist and counterfactual-review studies independently corroborate that manuscript-only LLM review can miss serious flaws, but they are not replications of artifact-aware review.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong that manuscript quality can mask artifact integrity problems and reviewer severity drifts substantially across reviewer identities.
scope_limits: Artifact-aware reviewers are themselves LLM agents and are not a scientific truth oracle.
Human meta-review focuses heavily on objectively checkable integrity, not comprehensive novelty/significance truth.
Hard integrity autorejection is a proposed transfer, not directly tested in the cited experiment.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for artifact-aware review surfacing integrity failures; C for the added hard-autoreject rule. Bundled candidate graded B overall.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Untested. O-specific use should preserve immutable evidence and compare artifact-aware versus report-only evaluation on matched held-out O outputs before treating a gate as validated.

source.title: How Far Are We From True Auto-Research?

assessments.primary_source_quality: Primary preprint with released run artifacts.
assessments.quantitative_result: The paper reports revision-round score changes by stage: e.g. Claude Code idea +2.1 average, experiment +2.2, paper +0.0; Codex idea +0.4, experiment +2.0, paper +1.5; Kimi Code idea +3.0, experiment +2.2, paper +1.6. Self-refinement used roughly 3%-8% of wall time.
assessments.matched_baseline: Weak for causal inference. Revision occurs conditionally below threshold and there is no randomized no-refinement control for the same state.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Low-to-moderate. Stage heterogeneity in internal gate-score response is clear, but improvement in true scientific quality attributable to refinement is not established.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Run trackers and artifacts are reported released, supporting reanalysis.
assessments.external_replication: None identified for the exact stage-specific intervention.
assessments.failure_evidence: Useful evidence that refinement can be neutral or degradative at some stages, especially Claude Code paper revision, but selection effects remain.
scope_limits: Endpoint is framework gate score, not independent scientific outcome.
Agent and stage effects may not transfer to O.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: C+ for stage-heterogeneous score response; not a causal proof of refinement benefit.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Requires randomized or otherwise matched O-specific operator ablations on downstream held-out outcomes before retention.

source.title: How Far Are We From True Auto-Research?

assessments.primary_source_quality: Primary preprint with per-domain H100/A6000 results and released harness/artifacts.
assessments.quantitative_result: All 8 GPU seeds were rerun with Codex on 8xH100 for 3 trials each with budget matched to 1xA6000 runs. Mean artifact-aware PR score was 4.26 on H100 versus 4.50 on A6000, delta -0.24; per-domain deltas ranged +0.22 to -1.00.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good within the tested setup: same agent and eight GPU-domain seeds with budget matching; hardware changes substantially, though stochastic research trajectories and reviewer-score endpoints remain.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for the narrow null/negative claim that more hardware did not improve the measured ResearchArena quality endpoint in this Codex setup. It does not isolate 'experiment design' as the unique causal bottleneck.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Reported harness and artifacts improve reproducibility; no independent replication checked.
assessments.failure_evidence: Direct null/negative scaling result within one agent and eight seeds.
scope_limits: One agent/model and eight GPU-domain seeds.
Outcome is artifact-aware reviewer score, not a direct real-world scientific endpoint.
Supports 'compute was not sufficient here', not 'compute is generally irrelevant' or 'experiment design is proven sole bottleneck'.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for the tested budget-matched hardware-scaling null result.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: O should use it only as evidence to test bottleneck class before increasing compute; it is not evidence that O would fail to benefit from compute.

source.title: BadScientist: Can a Research Agent Write Convincing but Unsound Papers that Fool LLM Reviewers?

assessments.primary_source_quality: High: peer-reviewed ACL 2026 paper with a defined threat model, calibrated review setup, formal aggregation analysis, and controlled mitigation dataset.
assessments.quantitative_result: Fabricated papers reached acceptance up to 82%. Concern-acceptance conflict remained large. In the mitigation comparison, Review-with-Detection raised panel integrity concern rate from 57.3% to 86.0% while calibrated acceptance rose 28.0% to 44.0% and probability-consistent acceptance 37.0% to 58.0%. On the 100-paper detection set, o3 ReD accuracy was 67% versus 50% random, while several other model configurations were near chance.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for showing that merely adding a detection subtask does not mechanically couple concern to recommendation: same model/rubric baseline versus ReD is directly compared on the controlled set. No matched experiment of the proposed hard gate/weighting rule itself is provided.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the failure premise (awareness can increase without stricter decisions); weak for efficacy of the proposed gate. A hard or weighted integrity gate is recommended/inferred rather than tested against false-rejection and scientific-quality endpoints.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Paper exposes framework details and project page; this pass verified the numeric tables from the authoritative ACL PDF. Full independent reproduction was not performed.
assessments.external_replication: No direct replication of the exact concern-to-gate intervention. Separate 2026 TACL counterfactual-review work reports automatic reviewers often fail to react to faulty research logic, providing broad independent corroboration of reviewer-validity weakness but not the same intervention.
assessments.failure_evidence: Very strong within paper-only review scope: awareness and acceptance can be behaviorally decoupled, and multi-reviewer aggregation can be precise while invalid.
scope_limits: Paper-only, single-pass review with no code execution or artifact verification.
Fabrication attacks were presentation manipulations without prompt injection/collusion and were not adaptively optimized against reviewer feedback.
Acceptance calibration is specific to the paper's ICLR-2025-based setup.
The proposed hard decision gate may introduce false rejections; that tradeoff is not experimentally established.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for the failure claim that stated integrity concern is not reliably decision-coupled in the tested LLM-review setup; C for the untested hard-gating remedy. Bundled mechanism graded B-.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: O-specific typed blocking/weighting remains unvalidated until evaluated on O outputs with false-positive, false-negative, and downstream-decision controls.

cross_candidate_conclusions: The strongest directly supported intervention in this batch is executable artifact access/probing, but its effect is conditional on probe choice and still lacks independent replication.
Artifact-aware review has substantial empirical support for exposing integrity problems, but the worker's additional hard-autoreject policy is a transfer proposal rather than a tested component.

BadScientist provides unusually strong evidence for an evaluator action-gap: verbal concern is not equivalent to decision control. It does not establish that a particular hard gate is optimally calibrated.

The stage-specific self-refinement proposal is substantially weaker than the raw score deltas may suggest because revisions are threshold-triggered and evaluated on internal gate scores without a randomized no-refinement control.
The H100 scaling result is credible narrow negative evidence and should remain narrowly scoped: more hardware did not improve this tested Codex/ResearchArena reviewer-score endpoint.
